title: Git Version Control Basics
description: Learn standard commands for initializing, cloning, staging, committing, and branching in Git.

tasks.prompt: Initialize a new local Git repository in the current folder.
tasks.explanation: 'git init' creates a hidden '.git' directory so this folder can track history.

tasks.prompt: Set the local user name for this repository to 'Ada Lovelace'.
tasks.hint: Use: git config user.name "Ada Lovelace" (or git config --local user.name "Ada Lovelace")
tasks.explanation: Repository-local user.name stamps commits in this repo with an author name without changing your machine-wide Git identity.

tasks.prompt: Set the local user email for this repository to 'ada@example.com'.
tasks.hint: Use: git config user.email "ada@example.com" (or git config --local user.email "ada@example.com")
tasks.explanation: Repository-local user.email completes the author identity for commits in this repo without a --global machine-wide change.

tasks.hint: Use git clone followed by the URL: 'git clone https://github.com/user/repo.git'
tasks.explanation: 'git clone' downloads a full copy of a remote repository, including its history, into a new local directory.

tasks.prompt: Check the status of tracked/untracked changes in the current branch.
tasks.explanation: 'git status' shows untracked, modified, and staged files relative to the last commit so you know what would be committed.

tasks.prompt: Append a line containing '*.log' to the '.gitignore' file so Git ignores log files.
tasks.explanation: Appending '*.log' to .gitignore tells Git to skip matching files so they are not staged by accident; >> keeps any existing ignore rules.

tasks.prompt: Stage all modified and untracked files in the current directory.
tasks.hint: Use git add followed by dot: 'git add .'
tasks.explanation: 'git add .' stages all directory changes, marking them as ready for the next commit.

tasks.prompt: Commit the staged changes with the description message 'initial commit'.
tasks.hint: Use commit command with message flag: 'git commit -m "initial commit"'
tasks.explanation: 'git commit -m' records the staged snapshot in history with a short message describing the change.

tasks.prompt: Create and immediately switch to a new branch named 'feature'.
tasks.hint: Use git checkout with -b, or git switch with -c: 'git checkout -b feature'
tasks.explanation: Creating with -b/-c makes a new branch pointer and moves HEAD there so your next commits land on 'feature'.
